THE TEN TOOLS AN AGENT ACTUALLY DRIVES, PROFILED ON THE RELEASE BINARY: FOUR ORIENTATION ROLLUPS ARE 35 OF 40 SECONDS, THREE CAUSES ARE LOCATED, FOUR HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED — AND THE THIRD CAUSE MULTIPLIES THE OTHER TWO ACROSS A SESSION, ~10 TIMES A SESSION, MEASURED. Taken 2026-09-05, reflow2-mcp 0.47.1 release, stdio direct, median of 3 warm runs after one cold. Tool set from `tools/surface_usage.py` (9,998 real calls, 61 sessions). Load 1.8-4.2 on 4 cores; RATIOS and SUBTRACTIONS are what this rests on.

  RELEASE, LIVE store (104 MB / 22 SST, 3709 n / 18101 e)   cold ms   warm ms   bytes
    loop_status                                             11,754    12,502   4,328
    open_questions                                          10,553     9,670     246
    graph_report                                             7,654     7,377  18,431
    detect_defects                                           5,952     5,633  44,263
    claim_report                                             2,505     2,558   2,231
    detect_gaps                                              1,661     1,760   6,642
    search_design                                           12,481         2.7  2,860
    what_next                                                  350       368   2,893
    describe_schema                                            3.8       3.6  45,644
    get_node                                                   1.6       1.3     452
    TOTAL warm                                                        39,877 127,990

THE STORY IS LATENCY, NOT BYTES. Point reads are 1-4 ms; four rollups are 35 of 40 s.

⭐⭐ CAUSE 3 — THE MULTIPLIER: EVERY READ AFTER A WRITE RUNS A FULL loop_status TO APPEND A ONE-LINE HINT. `service.rs:3731 read_loop_hint` computes `g.loop_status()` and caches it keyed on `write_gen`; `write_gen.fetch_add` at `service.rs:3647` is in the single write-lock path, so EVERY write invalidates it and the NEXT read of ANY kind recomputes. Measured on a scratch copy, alternating create_node / get_node: reads after a write 7,672 / 7,770 / 6,719 ms; the writes 82-127 ms; the second read 1-2 ms. TEN CALLS 30.3 s, 29.9 s OF IT HIDDEN. Server log silent throughout — reflow2's own rollup, not storage. `describe_schema` (no store) cold 6 ms and `claim_report` (no hint) show no spike: the subtraction that located it.

⭐ HOW OFTEN, COUNTED FROM 61 REAL SESSIONS rather than estimated: classifying every recorded transition by the toolsnaps' `readOnlyHint`, WRITE→READ = 579 of 6,974 transitions (8.3%) = **9.5 PER SESSION**. Sessions are ~80% writes (4,901 write→write), so the hint fires at run boundaries. HIDDEN loop_status PER SESSION: 9.5 x 7.7 s = 1.2 MINUTES measured on scratch; 9.5 x ~12 s = 1.9 MINUTES on the live daemon (inferred from the measured live loop_status). An earlier draft of this fact said 'dozens of times'; the count is 9.5 and this supersedes it. Commonest boundaries: `authored_by→loop_status` 36 (pays loop_status TWICE — once for the hint, once for the call), `set_artifact_checksums→export_graph` 36, `add_change_event→propagate_change` 23, `add_decision→get_node` 19, `create_edges→loop_status` 14.

⭐ CAUSE 1 — WHAT THAT HIDDEN loop_status IS MADE OF: `open_defects()` UNCACHED. 5.2-5.8 s per run, `heal.rs:964`, no memoisation, TEN call sites; three are orientation rollups (`report.rs:853 loop_status_for`, `:1348 graph_report`, `:597 debt_since` — so `since_export: true` pays twice). Computed to produce a COUNT. 📌 THE HINT CACHE AT `service.rs:3731` IS ALREADY A write_gen-KEYED CACHE, so a generation-keyed memo of open_defects would reuse an accepted pattern, not introduce one.

⭐ CAUSE 2 — FIVE DEAD SCRATCH EXPORTS COST EVERY loop_status ~3.5 s. `sync_status` alone: 3,556 ms live (6 targets) vs 19 ms fresh (0). 53.7 MB parsed per call; five are one-off `/tmp` files from dead sessions — the SAME five whose false claims v0.47.1 fixed. The claim went, the read stayed.

TOGETHER, per write→read boundary on the live daemon: open_defects 5.8 + sync 3.6 + detect_gaps 1.8 + other ≈ 12 s, paid for a hint on a 452-byte read.

🛑 FOUR HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED, so nobody re-tests them: (a) STORE BLOAT — live 104 MB / 22 SST vs fresh 17 MB / 0 SST for identical content; every rollup within noise on the fresh store. (b) GRAPH GROWTH — v0.46.0 design (3% smaller) costs the same. (c) `rehydrate_gaps` PER GAP — `ask.rs:381` runs detect_gaps once. (d) CODE REGRESSION SINCE v0.46.0 — a v0.46.0 release binary on a store it wrote: open_questions 8,906, loop_status 6,857, detect_defects 5,053 — indistinguishable from 0.47.1. The recorded 2.95 s for open_questions was taken under conditions not reproduced here.

⚠️ TWO NEAR-MISSES KEPT: the v0.46.0 binary first refused a 0.47.1-written store with `-32602 tool not found` in 0.2 ms — without the profiler's ERR column that reads as a 10,000x win (`rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object`); and a 40-line cap on a log read hid the lines that mattered until re-pulled uncapped.

⚠️ STILL UNEXPLAINED: open_questions ~7 s over 57 Questions (~123 ms each) beyond detect_gaps; needs a timing probe inside `detect.rs:1765`. ALSO OBSERVED, UNINVESTIGATED: tantivy runs a COMMIT and GARBAGE-COLLECT on every read-only open (~300 ms, deleting segment files).

📌 BOUNDS. One machine, 4 cores, desktop load floor ~2, release, stdio. Instruments: `tools/agent_surface_profile.py`, `tools/time_one_tool.py`; transition count from `tools/surface_usage.py --json` classified by `tools/toolsnaps/*.json` readOnlyHint.
